newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Challenge for Gulf LNG to enter Europe - BP analyst.
newsitem.headline: Challenge for Gulf LNG to enter Europe - BP analyst.

text.p: Gulf liquefied natural (LNG) gas projects should seek Asian markets as European prices are low for such exporters, British Petroleum Co Plc's chief economist said on Tuesday.

Peter Davies told a BP seminar in Kuwait that the several regional multi-billion-dollar LNG projects face a "major challenge" by trying to secure European customers who are "surrounded by a gas lake".
He said costly Gulf LNG projects would not be justified if they sought to enter European markets where piped gas is available at $2.5 per million British thermal units (Mbtu).
Some Gulf LNG producers see a price of around $3.5 per Mbtu, similar to an agreement between Qatar and Japan, as fair and covers the huge production and sea transportation costs.
They argue that about 3,000 miles (4,800 km) lie between them and European markets while Japan is some 7,000 miles (11,200 km) away.
But Europe has access to cheap natural gas by pipeline from sources such as North Africa, the North Sea and Russia.

Qatar, which has the world's third largest gas reserves, Oman and neighbouring Yemen all have ambitious LNG projects and have so far been negotiating mainly with Asian customers while West European consumers are baulking at what they see as high prices.
